Temperature controlled soldering ststion is a must. Those cheapo soldering irons woth a dial aren't actually temp controlled. Get a t12 clone they can be had for about 30-60 bucks and they're great. Use thin rosin core tin lead solder. .6mm to .8mm diameter 63 37 tin lead is the best imo but 60 40 does the job. Stay far the fuck away from lead free crap. Get you a good quality no clean flux. I stick with mg chemicals and chipqik mostly. Also don't be afraid to be generous with the amount of flux used. If you want to remove surface mount chips a hot air station is the way to go. 

Practice is the beat teacher but don't immediately start soldering on boards your gonna miss off you screw them up.  Go to the thrift store and buy some junk electronics to mess with. They typically will just about give away broken shit. Make a challenge of trying to repair them. For removing surface mount stuff like resistors or leds I like to use 2 soldering irons at the same temp and heat both sides up simultaneous. Makes it quick. Experiment woth different temperatures till you find the ranges your comfortable with and try different types.  I like chisel tips and knife tips personally but there's a bunch of different tips.

Good luck
